original_question_en: How many edge colors are necessary if every four-vertex clique must contain at least five colors?
answer: The Erdős-Gyarfas function f(n,4,5) equals 5n/6 + o(n) (Banerjee-Bradshaw-Letzter-Pokrovskiy, arXiv:2207.02920).
statement: f(n,4,5) = 5n/6 + o(n), i.e. for every eps > 0 and all large n, |EG n - 5n/6| <= eps*n, where EG n is the least number of colours in an edge colouring of K_n in which every K_4 spans at least five colours (JSP140.FiveSixth JSP140.EG, JSP140.jsp_000140_target).
notes: Catalog statement recovered 2026-09-30. Round 2: build OK, 0 sorry/admit, partial_ok=true. Round 2 proved the classical counting bound in full (Counting.lean): the structural theorem nb_eq_singleton (every colour class of an admissible colouring is a disjoint union of single edges and two-edge paths), the degree-sum identity, the disjointness of the two-edge paths (2|A| <= |B|), the counting lemma 3*|E_i| <= 2n, the partition of the edges by colour classes, and hence the classical Erdős-Gyárfás bound 3*(n-1) <= 4*k, i.e. f(n,4,5) >= 3(n-1)/4 (Counting.classical_lower_bound), plus the corollary fiveSixthLower_at_eighth: the lower half of the headline holds for every eps >= 1/8 and n >= 18. The key new structural lemma is classIn_avoid_in (ColorClass.lean), the round-1 blocker 1. Still missing for jsp_000140_main: the linear (round-robin) construction for the two-sided shape bound, and the BCDP22 sharpening 3/4 -> 5/6 (both eps-sides).
